features: The new portal is now the portal, at /portal. Old addresses, bookmarks and links in earlier emails still work: they open the matching page in the new portal. The classic portal stays available to administrators only, as a fallback.

Client version floor: the CLI warns as soon as your version is below the gateway's minimum, offers to upgrade on the spot, and tells long-running tunnels and the Inspector when the deadline approaches. The portal shows a banner, and you get one email when the warning window opens.
Portal: tunnel details can add and remove headers, override the rate limit, copy the URL and refresh. Header and rate-limit changes now reach tunnels served by a regional gateway too.

Portal: the dashboard has direct links to tokens, reservations and tunnels; admins get the reservations CSV, preferred domain and tour status in the user details, and the help panel links the Docker image and the documentation.

Single sign-on: your name comes from the identity provider at every sign-in. If the provider does not perform MFA, the gateway asks for your authenticator code; if it does, Account Settings says so instead of offering to set one up.

Install and upgrade now write the client straight into its install folder (~/liferay/lfr-tunnel) on every OS, instead of downloading it to a temporary folder first. If a download fails, the version you had is kept.

macOS: start at login now runs lfr-tunnel itself, not a copy named "Liferay Tunnel", and removes that copy if an earlier version left one. Uninstalling the service also removes the tray's start-at-login entry.
On an EDR-managed machine, including every Liferay machine, install with the native installer rather than Homebrew or Scoop. The InfoSec guide now has one table of install paths and exclusion rules.

Single sign-on: sign in with your organisation's identity provider (Liferay SSO on Liferay's gateway). Your account is matched by email address in any letter case, so an existing account stays yours, and SSO sign-ins now show under Last Seen.
Single sign-on: when the identity provider does not confirm your email address, the gateway can confirm it itself by emailing you a one-time link. After that, sign-ins go straight through.
Portal: every portal address now opens on one canonical host, so you are not asked to sign in again because you arrived on a different name.

CLI: `lfr-tunnel login` checks the token with the gateway before reporting success. It accepts a token pasted with quotes or a "Bearer " prefix, and gives up after 15 minutes instead of holding its port. If another login is already waiting, it says which process. The portal opens the create-token dialog for you.

CLI: a malformed -ports value is now refused instead of silently ignored, and the terminal and health check show the ports actually shared. Auto-discovery shares only the project's portal container, never Liferay Docker Manager's shared containers. If you share an LDM project that has an LCP.json, use LDM v2.26.11 or later.
Privacy: access tokens are removed from client logs before they are uploaded.
Admins: Audit Log export follows the active filter and sort, can export only the rows you select, and can anonymise the addresses in it. Actions on a user now always apply to that exact account.
Admins: each alert can now go to email, to Slack, or both. The owner sets this per alert in System Settings, so an alert handled in Slack no longer has to land in the inbox too.
Single sign-on: Portal V2 now offers the same "Continue with ..." sign-in as V1, and returns you to V2 afterwards. When a gateway is set to SSO-only, both portals hide the email sign-in form.
Single sign-on: on an SSO-only gateway, admins can no longer send email invitations and emailed sign-in links no longer work. New people join by signing in through the identity provider.
Security update: SSO sign-in now uses PKCE and a nonce, and only accepts an email address the identity provider has verified.

Analytics: Export PDF prints the wide sections (gateways, sessions, latency, node placement) on landscape pages, and charts are redrawn at their printed size instead of shrunk from the screen. Tested in Chrome.
Analytics: Personal Usage now says when you have no tunnel traffic in the period, instead of showing an empty section.
Admins: the sidebar now shows a count beside every approval queue -- pending registrations, extension requests and token permanence requests -- and it updates as soon as a request is decided.

Admins: admin alerts can now also be sent to a Slack channel, either by email to the channel or through the Liferay Tunnel Slack app. The owner chooses which in System Settings, and every alert type is covered.
Admins: unverified registrations are listed under Registrations in both portals, and only registrations waiting for a decision are counted.
Security update: library updates close published security advisories. Nothing changes in how you use the tunnel.
